summary: Staged steganographic dropper writes disguised Windows executable to APPDATA on require()
details: img-to-native@1.0.0 presents itself as an image-conversion library but its index.js runs a top-level IIFE on require() that polls %TMP%/._cif_data for up to 120 seconds, locates a payload concealed after a PNG IEND chunk and a '//BIN//' sentinel, base64-decodes it, AES-256-CBC decrypts it with a hardcoded key derived from the string 'malfexteam2027', and writes the resulting binary to %APPDATA%/Microsoft/Windows/node_runtime_helper.exe with mode 0700 — a Microsoft-branded path chosen to blend into system directories. The package declares a runtime dependency on cdn-img-fetch ^1.0.0 but never requires it in code; instead it waits for that sibling package to stage the encrypted PNG carrier at the polled temp path, forming a split fetcher/decryptor dropper across two packages. No image-conversion functionality is present; the advertised API is a cover story for the drop-and-materialize chain.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
